message: Reviewer's read-only `sed -n` on .kukulu/cleanroom/log.jsonl was denied as a protected path, while a `grep` on the same file a call earlier was allowed; the skill tells the reviewer to read that log's denied entries, so the read-only form costs a retry through the Read tool.

Round 1's unblock reason for P1-10 (do not declare LZ4_decompress_safe_usingDict; build dict_block without it) lived only in PROGRESS.md, while PLAN.md's P1-10 body still said a missing usingDict blocks. The implementer did the exact forbidden thing (declared it in ffi.rs), re-blocked within a minute, and 17 reopened tasks were skipped again, costing a whole round.

The clean-room guard denied a read-only `sed -n 2910,2990p mcp/server.mjs` (cwd in the plugin cache) as "protected path: <plugin dir>/2910,2990p", resolving sed's script argument as a path. I wanted to learn whether kukulu_task_next shows unblock reasons to the implementer; I did not retry another way.

Reviewer's read-only `sed -n '593,644p' .kukulu/cleanroom/log.jsonl | node -e ...` was denied as a protected path, while a `grep` on the same log was allowed a moment earlier. The skill tells the reviewer to read denied entries and scan the log since lastReviewCommit, but gives no sanctioned read path for it; I did not retry another way and relied on kukulu_status's denied count instead.

kukulu_mutate with targeted 'cargo' and a list filter expands to `cargo test --workspace 'a' 'b'`, which cargo rejects (it takes one TESTNAME), so the result came back inconclusive. The tool offers list filters but the configured targeted command cannot take more than one; one mutate call was wasted.

Reviewer's `sed -n` on the Kukulu plugin's mcp/server.mjs was denied as a protected path (a grep on the same file had just been allowed). I wanted to learn how kukulu_review_submit treats a CHANGES REQUESTED with zero tasks when the only open item is an owner-blocked task; the skill does not say, so the reviewer has to guess.

kukulu_review_submit refused CHANGES REQUESTED with no tasks and no unblock, but the skill forbids APPROVED while a task is blocked. When the only open item is an owner-only block (P1-10), the reviewer has no sanctioned verdict and must find a fix task to queue; the skill should say what to submit in that case (for example, halt for the owner).

kukulu_verify on a result path that runs make fuzz-run (3600 s) was aborted by the MCP idle timeout of 1800 s with no progress output, though the underlying process kept running; the verify result never came back and I had to poll for the result file by hand. Long-run extraVerify commands need progress notifications or a longer MCP tool timeout.

The guard refused a read-only `sed -n` on docs/spec/lz4_Frame_format.md as a "protected path" write, though `grep` on the same file was allowed a call earlier; reading docs/spec is a permitted input, so the reviewer switched to the Read tool.
